unit.why: A teaching quoted from R. Yitzhak Eizik of Komarno's Netiv Mitzvotekha frames a brief anecdote: R. Levi Yitzhak of Berdichev, in Warsaw, warmly urges a coarse, lowly man named Binesh to cleave to God, and onlookers laugh.
unit.boundary_note: anecdote embedded in a homiletic quotation; previous and next divisions are separate items

stories.start_quote: בסה״ק נתיב מצותיך למורינו הרה״ק מוהרי״א מקומארנא
stories.end_quote: להשפיע לכל העולם מאור הזה וכו׳ עכ״ל הק׳
stories.summary_en: Quoting the Komarner: a true tzaddik receives everyone, even the lowliest, with joy. As an example, R. Levi Yitzhak of Berdichev in Warsaw lovingly urged a coarse man, Binesh, to bind himself to God in devekut, which seemed laughable to others, even to pious tzaddikim.

tags.why: the anecdote is wrapped in a quoted homiletic teaching about the tzaddik's nature
